articles.title: How to Play the Grand Theft Auto Games in Order
articles.summary: How to navigate every GTA timeline ahead of GTA 6.
articles.body:
It’s hard to talk about modern video games without mentioning the influence of Grand Theft Auto. Rockstar’s iconic crime franchise has grown from a controversial PlayStation 1 classic to a universally recognised cultural behemoth, with its most recent entry, Grand Theft Auto 5, becoming one of the best-selling games of all time .

However, the series didn’t grow into a landmark success overnight. Rockstar has been slowly building its iconic crime series for over two decades, creating hyper-immersive open worlds that players explore for years after their release. With over sixteen Grand Theft Auto games dropping since the franchise began in 1997, new players are probably wondering where to start.

To help you get stuck in, we’ve listed every GTA game in chronological order so you can plot the best route through the timeline of this crime-riddled world. Until we finally get our hands on GTA 6 , at least.

There are a total of 16 games in the Grand Theft Auto series – eleven on home consoles, one on PC and four on handheld devices. The next Grand Theft Auto game, GTA 6, is set to release in November 2026.

Before we dive into the list, it’s first worth noting an important detail about the overall continuity of Grand Theft Auto. As confirmed by Rockstar back in 2011, the GTA series is split into three unique timelines: the 2D timeline, the 3D timeline and the HD timeline. Although events in these timelines might be similar or even identical, Rockstar doesn’t consider all of them canon to each other. As such, we’ll separate the games into their respective universes.

If you're wanting to get into the Grand Theft Auto games before GTA 6 arrives, you will likely want to start with the latest in the series: GTA 5. You can certainly go back to previous games, but GTA 5 is a masterpiece in it's own right and is playable pretty much everywhere. You can also take advantage of GTA Online for multiplayer.

Otherwise, we're pretty close to that GTA 6 finish line, so if you happen to have a console, I wouldn't hold out on being a part of one of the biggest game launches of all time.

Grand Theft Auto 6 (Physical - Code in a Box)

Below, we’ll list the Grand Theft Auto games from the 2D universe. These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

The second expansion released for the original Grand Theft Auto, Grand Theft Auto: London 1961 is one of only two GTA releases to not hit a PlayStation console, with the DLC only available to PC players.

The mission pack acts as a prequel to Grand Theft Auto’s first expansion, Grand Theft Auto: London 1969. It follows a nameless criminal rising through the ranks of the London crime families by completing jobs for a mobster called Harold Cartwright.

The first expansion for the original Grand Theft Auto, Grand Theft Auto: London 1969 marked the series’ first visit to London.

The tale follows a nameless British criminal who fights against various crime syndicates while building their legend on the city’s streets. These include Harold Cartwright’s gang, which the player joins forces with in Grand Theft Auto: London 1961, as well as a pair of sinister crime lords known as the Crisp Twins.

The first entry in the mainline series, Grand Theft Auto follows the adventures of a nameless protagonist as they make their mark on the criminal underworlds of three locations: Liberty City, San Andreas and Vice City.

Set in 1997, the criminal’s adventures see them complete bank heists, assassinations and getaways, building their reputation while aiding various sinister gangs. Along the way, they meet a host of high-ranking criminals, including Robert Seragliano, El Burro and Uncle Fu.

The second mainline entry in the series, Grand Theft Auto 2 is arguably the biggest departure for the series to date. Shifting away from the setting of the first GTA, it takes players to a nigh-on futuristic metropolis known as Anywhere City, which bears no striking resemblance to any other location in the series.

The adventure follows a criminal named Claude Speed, who works with various crime syndicates around Anywhere City to make money and earn respect. The game’s position on the timeline is tricky, mainly as in-game references allude to it taking place in both 1999 and 2013. Regardless, it’s the final game in the 2D timeline.

Below, we’ll list the Grand Theft Auto games from the 3D universe. These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

A prequel to Grand Theft Auto: Vice City , the PSP’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories takes place in 1984 and follows US military soldier Victor Vance who, after being framed by his sergeant, is dishonorably discharged.

Fresh out of a job, he decides to enter Vice City’s underworld, quickly becoming the head of a crime family with the help of his brother, Lance. The pair embark on an adventure to disrupt Vice City’s crime scene, meeting and recruiting a variety of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City’s supporting characters along the way. By the time the game wraps up, Vic’s story catches up with the beginning of Vice City.

The fourth mainline iteration of the series, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City takes place in 1986; two years after Vice City Stories. It follows Tommy Verceti, a notorious gangster from Liberty City who is sent to Vice City to oversee the expansion of his boss’ drug trade after being released from jail.

Tommy lands in hot water after a supposedly simple drug deal goes horribly wrong. Losing the drugs and money exchanged in the deal, Tommy is given one last chance to make things right.

To redeem himself, he dives into the seedy underbelly of Vice City, allying with Lance Vance to take on its various crime families and find the drugs and money stolen from him. As he becomes a bigger name around Vice City, he slowly creates a growing criminal empire, which doesn’t go unnoticed by his former employers.

The fifth mainline iteration of the series, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas tells the story of Carl ‘CJ’ Johnson and the Grove Street Families.

Set in 1992, San Andreas follows CJ as he returns to Los Santos after his mother is killed in a drive-by meant to assassinate his brother. Reuniting with his friends, family and local gang, The Grove Street Families, it doesn’t take long for CJ to get stuck back into the criminal underworld, vowing to get revenge on the gang that murdered his mother.

While CJ attempts to rebuild the Grove Street gang’s former glory, it becomes clear that something shady is happening behind the scenes. Pursued by a crooked cop named Officer Tenpenny, CJ deals with betrayal, corrupt law enforcement and the various factions vying for control of Los Santos and the neighboring cities of San Fierro and Las Venturas.

4. Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

Set in 1998, Liberty City Stories acts as a prequel to Grand Theft Auto 3 and follows a gangster working for Salvatore Leone named Toni Cipriani. Returning to Liberty City after fleeing to Italy to escape the repercussions of assassinating a member of the mafia, Toni gets stuck back in working for his former boss.

Along the way, he meets several high-level mafia contacts and climbs through the ranks of Sal’s gang, murdering rival crime lords and assisting Leone’s attempts to gain political sway with the mayor. The story concludes with Salvatore Leone’s family standing as one the most powerful crime syndicates in Liberty City, setting up the events of Grand Theft Auto 3.

Taking place in 2000, Grand Theft Auto Advance was a Grand Theft Auto 3 prequel released on the Gameboy Advance. It follows a criminal named Mike as he attempts to get revenge for the death of his partner, Vinnie.

Deciding to leave Liberty City and find new opportunities elsewhere, the story begins with Mike and Vinnie completing jobs for the mafia in an attempt to tie up loose ends and fund their escape. However, the plan falls apart when Vinnie is killed with a car bomb, driving Mike to find and kill his murderers. In pursuit of vengeance, Mike teams with various Grand Theft Auto 3 characters, including 8-Ball and Asuka Kasen.

The final entry in the timeline but the first game of the 3D era by release date, Grand Theft Auto 3 takes place in 2001 and follows a new Claude, a bank robber that’s shot and left for dead by his girlfriend, Catalina, during a heist.

Claude survives but is arrested and sentenced to life in jail. However, while en route to prison, Claude manages to escape after the Columbian Cartel raided his convoy in search of another prisoner. Fleeing the scene, Claude is soon inducted into the criminal underworld of Liberty City, working with the mafia, the yakuza and various other syndicates.

Although he rises to become one of the city’s most notorious gangsters, Claude’s goal quickly becomes one of vengeance, as his path eventually crosses with Catalina, setting up an inevitable confrontation between the former couple.

Below, we’ll list the Grand Theft Auto games from the HD universe. These blurbs contain mild spoilers for each game, including characters, settings, and story beats.

The first game of the HD era, Grand Theft Auto 4 takes place in 2008 and follows an Eastern European ex-soldier named Niko Bellic as he makes his way to Liberty City. Coming to America to reunite with his cousin, Roman Bellic, who has allegedly found fortune after moving to Liberty City, Niko is shocked to find Roman is actually broke, living in a cockroach-infested apartment and running a failing business.

It doesn’t take long for Niko to find work and amass cash through less-than-legal means, meeting and befriending an arms dealer named Little Jacob and working off Roman’s debts with a Russian loan shark named Vlad Glebov. However, after discovering that Vlad has been sleeping with Roman’s girlfriend, Niko kills him, sparking a chain of events which puts him and Roman in the sights of the Russian mafia.

To survive, Niko allies with the crime families of Liberty City, where he becomes tangled in their politics and becomes one of the city’s most feared criminals. All the while, Niko has an ulterior motive, wanting to track down and murder a former comrade from his days in the military that double-crossed him and his squad.

2. Grand Theft Auto: The Lost and The Damned

Set during the events of Grand Theft Auto 4, The Lost and the Damned was GTA 4’s first expansion. It follows Johnny Klebitz, the Vice President of a revered motorcycle gang called The Lost MC.

Released from a long stint in rehab, the story opens with The Lost MC’s President, Billy Grey, returning to the gang and reassuming his position as its leader. During his time away, Johnny led The Lost MC, forming a truce with the gang’s main rivals, The Angels of Death. Once reinstated, Billy and Johnny begin to clash after Billy orders The Lost to break the truce with the Angels of Death, starting a ruthless gang war.

As the two gangs battle it out, Billy begins to lead The Lost down a self-destructive path, guiding his brothers into increasingly dangerous situations. With civil war brewing in the group, Johnny is forced to consider where his loyalty lies.

3. Grand Theft Auto: The Ballad of Gay Tony

The second of GTA 4’s expansions, The Ballad of Gay Tony also takes place alongside the core Grand Theft Auto campaign. The story follows bodyguard Luis Lopez as he tries to save the life of his boss and legendary nightclub owner, Tony Prince.

Although Tony is a fixture of Liberty City’s nightlife scene, his businesses are failing. To make matters worse, he’s also in debt to the Ancelotti crime family, who are ready to collect what they’re owed. Swearing to help his boss, Luis tries to square Tony’s debts, helping out his various criminal acquaintances.

It all crescendos with a risky plan from Tony, who decides to acquire millions of dollars worth of smuggled diamonds and exchange them in a deal. However, the plan falls apart, leading Luis on a wild goose chase around Liberty City in an attempt to retrieve the diamonds and keep Tony’s debts from catching up with him.

Taking place in 2009, Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars tells the story of Huang Lee, the son of a murdered Triad leader who is tasked with flying to Liberty City to deliver an ancient sword to his uncle.

After arriving in Liberty City, Huang is ambushed, with his attackers stealing the sword and shooting Huang. Believing him dead, they dump his body, allowing Huang to escape alive. Reuniting with his uncle, Huang embarks on an adventure to track down the sword and deliver it back to the Triads. Along the way, he works with various gangs and the FIB, learning that the sword’s theft may have been an inside job.

Although it’s difficult to judge where exactly it falls on the timeline, Grand Theft Auto Online begins shortly before Grand Theft Auto 5 and has, over the course of ten years of updates, shifted to a period of time long after the game’s main campaign.

The core story follows a player-created criminal that heads to Los Santos to find fortune, reputation and fame, creating factions, buying property and taking part in criminal ventures. The story has evolved over the years, with one of the latest updates revisiting the character of Franklin years after the events of Grand Theft Auto V , as he tasks the player with helping him in his business ventures.

Set in 2013, Grand Theft Auto 5 follows the story of three criminals: Franklin, Michael and Trevor. After staging his death during a bank robbery in the small town of North Yankton, Michael Townley enters a witness protection programme, moving to the sunny city of Los Santos to live a life of luxury in a giant mansion with his family.

However, he’s lured out of retirement when he meets Franklin Clinton , an ambitious small-time criminal sent to repossess Michael’s son’s car. Forming a friendship, Michael begins to mentor Franklin, eventually leading the pair to rob a jewelry store to pay off a local crime lord. However, the act doesn’t go unnoticed.

On the outskirts of Los Santos , Michael’s former friend and criminal associate, Trevor Phillips, watches a clip of the heist on the news. Realizing that his seemingly dead partner is still alive in Los Santos, Trevor heads to the city, joining Michael and Franklin to stage various elaborate heists. However, Trevor’s animosity towards Michael’s betrayal begins to drive a wedge between the group, as tensions rise and the truth behind the pair’s past comes to light.

While Take-Two Interactive initially announced a fall 2025 release window , GTA 6 is now slated to be released on November 19, 2026. And Rockstar actually seems pretty confident in that date, having opened preorders for the game in late June. Those preorders confirmed the existence of separate Standard and Ultimate editions , as well as the fact that the game won't include a physical disc , at least at launch. Rockstar has also confirmed the game will only be playable on consoles at launch. Nonetheless, it's already become one of the best-selling games of the year .

The game's reveal trailer showed off a fictionalized version of Florida (including Vice City) known in-game as Leonida , as well as our two criminal protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. A second trailer (which Rockstar called the "biggest video launch of all time" ) features a mix of cinematics and gameplay . And, most recently, we got to see a full 30-minute gameplay preview event. This may be one of the biggest game releases to date , and we're all hoping it's worth the wait.

articles.title: Heads Up: GTA 6 Preloads Begin November 12
articles.summary: If you're already plotting how to ditch work for a week in November to play GTA 6, you'll want to make sure to preload the game on your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S. Here's when you'll be able to.
articles.body:
I know a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6-related news is dropping today, but I wanted to remind/tell you about what to expect if you preorder. Preorders are live now , and the game will be released on November 19. But if you preorder, you’ll be able to download a copy onto your PS5 or Xbox Series S|X starting November 12 , according to Rockstar . That way you’ll be able to start playing the moment it’s released.

Grand Theft Auto 6 (Physical - Code in a Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition (Digital)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - PS5 Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Xbox Physical (Code in Box)

Grand Theft Auto 6 - Ultimate Edition Upgrade

That preload date works for both digital and “physical” preorders. I put the word physical in scare quotes because, while you do get a physical box, it doesn’t include a disc. Physical copies of GTA 6 are a code in a box. But that box will ship to you on November 12, at which point you can enter the code into your PS5 or Xbox Series X|S to download the game.

If you haven’t already preordered GTA 6 and you want to take advantage of the early preload situation, you’ll have to decide whether to buy it in digital or physical format . You’ll also have to decide whether you want the $79.99 standard edition or the $99.99 ultimate edition, the latter of which it turns out most people are preordering . Note that there’s no physical version of the ultimate edition, but you can buy the “Ultimate Edition Upgrade” for $20 on the PlayStation Store or Xbox Store.

All preorders come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+. Note that the GTA+ subscription auto-renews, so you’ll want to go ahead and set a reminder to cancel if you don’t want to continue paying for it. Here’s what’s in the Vintage Vice City Pack:

'55 VAPID STANIER: Cruise Shore Drive in this classic sedan and store it just a stone's throw from the glistening sands of Ocean Beach in the Shore Court garage, complete with a weapon locker plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods to be fenced.

OUTFITS AND HAIRSTYLES: Dress for excess with Jason’s effortlessly chic linen suit in vintage pastel, complemented by the cut and coif of the decade of decadence. Show everyone the world is yours in Lucia’s red sequin mini dress and curls.

EXCLUSIVE WEAPON PATTERN: Adorn most guns with a tropical pattern inspired by Tommy Vercetti's iconic palm tree button-up.

The Vintage Vice City Pack is included with all digital purchases of Grand Theft Auto VI made prior to November 20, 2026.

The ultimate edition includes the base game, plus a ton of extra digital content that Rockstar says is “threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s story.” Here’s what’s included:

’95 GROTTI CHEETAH: Grotti's signature mid '90s sports car and ode to Shore Drive, the ’95 Grotti Cheetah is complete with a minimalist, retro-futuristic livery and available to punctuate later-stage action.

HAWK & LITTLE MORGAN REVOLVER: His and hers versions of this powerful revolver with classic Vice City stylings sourced from the Vercetti Estate, including palm-tree-etched grips, engraved detailing, and high-performance scope.

PERSONALIZED WEAPON VARIANTS: Personalized sidearms with detailed engravings for Jason's Girardi ES9 pistol and Lucia's Klose K17 pistol.

VICE CITY STYLE: Whether poolside or side by side, Jason and Lucia can look the part with exclusive outfits, hairstyles, tattoos, and more.

JASON’S SAFEHOUSE VEHICLES: Switch gears and soak up the sun in an Army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle or Crest Kayak.

SHITZU SQUALO: Perfect for casting in Gambit Bay and reeling in catches of all sorts, this gradient pink and blue Squalo docked at Washington Beach is made open-ocean-ready with an explosives-laden weapons crate.

'67 VAPID DOMINATOR BUGGY & GARAGE: A Mud Club monster offering impressive off-road handling for the backwoods of Mount Kalaga and beyond. Conveniently store it at the Paradise Garage in Watson Bay, which features a weapon locker plus a secure place to deposit stolen goods to be fenced.

articles.title: The Way You Steal Cars in GTA 6 Completely Changes the Game
articles.summary: Stealing cars is no longer a case of just tapping a button in GTA 6. Rockstar reveals how it has added “layers of stratification” to make the theft in Grand Theft Auto a little more challenging.
articles.body:
Ever since the first game launched back in 1997, Grand Theft Auto’s titular crime has been a fairly simple process: tap one button and someone else’s car is now yours. Almost 30 years later, GTA 6 is set to change that completely, introducing a tiered vehicle security system, a varied set of tools to steal them with, and new ways to profit from each theft directly. Let’s look at the details of how it all works in Rockstar’s latest, as well as theorise about what it could all mean for other styles of robbery, including liquor store hold-ups and big bank heists.

Long-term GTA fans will be more than familiar with how stealing a car has worked in the series thus far. You walk up to your desired wheels and simply press a button to open a door left carelessly unlocked, or smash through the window with your elbow to enter better secured vehicles. That simplicity won’t be going away completely in GTA 6, it appears, with older, less desirable vehicles still vulnerable to swift methods of entry, such as a quick slim jim forced into the window gap and under the lock. But other, much more high-end motors will come packed with added security layers that introduce new gameplay challenges, asking players to flex unfamiliar muscles when it comes to jacking cars.

“We have put some layers of stratification into the vehicles,” explains Rob Nelson, co-studio head of Rockstar North. “Previously, you could just press triangle to automatically hotwire and steal any vehicle that you wanted and take off. We felt like that left a lot of potential gameplay on the table, in terms of progression and decision-making for players. I think it gives all the vehicles more meaning, and you need to pay attention to what you’re doing a bit more.”

But how will you know which cars will be harder to crack than others? Well, apart from passing a quick eye test of being able to distinguish a rusty old white van from a straight off the production line Grotti sports car, you’ll need to take advantage of a new bit of GTA 6 tech: the WAINK scanner.

Get within range of any vehicle that takes your fancy, and you’ll be able to hold your device up to get all of the relevant information. Chief among these details are its security system and value. We don’t yet know how many car security tiers there’ll be, but what we do know is that some will be protected digitally, as GTA catches up with the modern age of electronic keys. That means you’ll need a digital key cloning device in order to unlock some car doors, but that piece of kit will come at a cost, with it needing to be acquired first. Some tools will only unlock after a certain point in the story, and it’s a clear sign that GTA 6 is aiming to evolve its gameplay opportunities over the course of the game. It’s all in service of adding levels of complexity to binary actions.

But technology can also work against you. Even if you manage to get behind the wheel of your chosen target, that car may be fitted with a tracker — some advanced versions of which reveal your location to law enforcement if you drive below a certain speed, meaning you need to put your foot down to avoid hearing sirens. Not only will it draw police attention your way if the car is reported as stolen, but, in theory, any prospective buyer worth its name in salt would want it removed before you cash in. This ties into another layer of GTA 6’s enhanced simulation – you’ll be able to visit a fence and sell any vehicle you’ve stolen. Yes, Rockstar is borrowing from its previous game, Red Dead Redemption 2, albeit you’ll be hunting metal beasts rather than taking down meaty big bucks for big bucks. And Arthur Morgan never had to worry about GPS trackers ruining the value of his finds.

But perhaps you aren’t stealing a car with pure profit foremost in mind, but instead just fancy making it your own. Well, the WAINK scanner (yes, it’s really called that and I have no idea what that acronym stands for right now) also tells you how much it will cost to register that car as your own. GTA 6 will allow Jason and Lucia to each own multiple personal vehicles, provided you have the cash and garage space.

Both of these new systems — tiered security and fencing — open up a whole new world of possibilities when it comes to mission design in GTA 6. Don’t be surprised to see more organic, emergent solutions to mission objectives appear as you play. For example, the simple fact that many cars can’t be instantly broken into and commandeered makes the act of escape an altogether more frantic endeavor. You might get lucky and slide into an unsecured sedan on the first try, but with the police at your back, you’re realistically not going to have the time to stop and scan the area for the perfect getaway vehicle. It all builds into Rockstar’s intention for you to spend more time scurrying away on foot or changing methods of transport on the fly, with the narrower Leonida streets helping generate exciting desperation and unexpected thrills.

“The streets in this game are narrower, and more realistic in terms of scale”, Nelson explains. “Which, in addition to all the density of the traffic on the roads, makes driving slightly more challenging and requires a bit of skill.”

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

That more organic approach to moment-to-moment action could extend to specific styles of mission, too. Not an insignificant amount of time in both GTA 5 and GTA Online is spent reclaiming cars for Simeon, Franklin’s original employer. These primarily serve as simple, introductory quests to the world of San Andreas and its gameplay fundamentals, but in GTA 6, the framework of similar jobs could become a lot more rewarding with these additional layers of complexity.

Rather than simply placing a marker on your map to drive to and demanding you deliver a predetermined vehicle back to whoever requires it, the possibilities have now opened up, thanks to the WAINK scanner. In theory, you could be asked to find a specific brand of car around the world, or one of a specific value, and use this newfound technology to go on a miniature treasure hunt. Doing so would embed us further into GTA 6’s world and allow us to spend less time following markers and traced lines along roads on a mini map. Being able to take this newly procured car to any fence on the map would also help mix things up, rather than the tedium that zooming along the same few streets back to Simeon’s in Los Santos could become.

But perhaps most exciting is how these systems could translate into GTA 6’s bigger, high-stakes missions. In theory, the back rooms of small stores could be easily broken into, with the minimal spoils waiting there, yours to take. But what about big banks or heavily guarded facilities? Surely some more advanced tech will need to be employed here to crack safes or bypass locked doors. If you don’t have the right tools for the job, such as the aforementioned key cloning device, then does that limit what you’ll take away from a score, or potentially make missions branch in interesting ways? These are all choices that will seemingly add up over the course of GTA 6, and the repercussions could range from short-term problems such as an increased wanted level, to permanently damaging Jason and Lucia’s relationship.

Stealing cars has been at the core of Grand Theft Auto for almost three decades now, but this fundamental change to how it all works is as exciting a change as Rockstar has made in that time. I can’t wait to get my hands on it and see for myself just how much it opens up its world and the possibilities within it.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: GTA VI al detalle: nuevas mecánicas y jugabilidad, HUD al estilo 'Red Dead' y el mapa de Leónida
articles.standfirst: El último metraje de la esperada obra de Rockstar Games revela un sinfín de novedades jugables
articles.summary: El último metraje de la esperada obra de Rockstar Games revela un sinfín de novedades jugables
articles.body: GTA VI: 'Una mirada extendida' nos ha dejado casi media hora de gameplay de la nueva obra de Rockstar, en el que podemos apreciar un montón de detalles de jugabilidad y del nuevo mundo en general que nos ofrece el videojuego más esperado de la historia. El análisis de estas secuencias de juego confirma una profunda evolución en las mecánicas de sigilo, la interacción con el entorno y una notable similitud entre los sistemas de supervivencia e inmersión vistos en Red Dead Redemption 2. Una de las grandes revelaciones se centra en la reestructuración del sistema de búsqueda policial. En plena persecución, los protagonistas pueden despistar a las autoridades adentrándose en aparcamientos y quemando su vehículo de escape mediante un cóctel molotov, lo que provoca la desaparición inmediata del icono del coche en el radar. En el plano jugable, la cooperación entre ambos delincuentes gana en fluidez: el sistema permitirá alternar entre Jason y Lucía en tiempo real con solo pulsar el botón R1, agilizando el ritmo tanto en misiones como en mundo abierto, aunque suponemos que esto estará delimitado en ciertas misiones, en las que tendrás que ir intercambiando con ellos simultáneamente. La interfaz de usuario adopta una clara herencia de las mecánicas de bienestar de Red Dead Redemption 2: - Tres barras de estado: Se incluye una barra de vida con segmento crítico, una barra de energía (stamina) y una nueva barra de cansancio o sueño, lo que apunta a la necesidad de descansar para mantener el rendimiento. - Gestión económica clásica: El HUD vuelve a diferenciar de forma visible en la esquina derecha entre el dinero en efectivo y el saldo disponible en la cuenta bancaria. - Rueda de armas de ocho huecos: Tres ranuras fijas quedan asignadas de inicio para pistola, combate cuerpo a cuerpo (puños) y prismáticos. En el cuadrante inferior izquierdo se integran pastillas y consumibles destinados a recuperar o sobrepotenciar la salud. - Rueda de accesorios y disfraces: Un nuevo menú radial permite equipar o retirar gafas, gorras y máscaras, sumando un icono con forma de percha pensado para cambiar de disfraz o atuendo sobre la marcha. La exposición en redes sociales también tendrá su peso dentro de la experiencia de juego. En una de las secuencias más surrealistas y dinámicas del metraje, Lucía descubre a una suerte de creador de contenido encerrado en el maletero de un vehículo robado, pero lejos de asustarse, el influencer retransmite la persecución policial en riguroso directo, mostrando las reacciones y los comentarios del chat en tiempo real en la esquina superior derecha de la pantalla. A esto se le suma la integración de las aplicaciones de mensajería instantánea, clave para la coordinación en las misiones entre ambos delincuentes. A través del teléfono móvil, los protagonistas se comunican en situaciones límite: el intercambio de mensajes sirve como nexo narrativo entre ambos, y, a través de ellos, es cuando ocurre un cambio inmediato de perspectiva jugable entre los dos. Más allá de los atracos, el metraje ilustra la enorme variedad de actividades que podrás realizar en Leónida. Los jugadores podrán desplazarse en patinete eléctrico, surcar las zonas pantanosas, entrenar con pesas en el gimnasio, jugar al baloncesto en casa, practicar buceo, pilotar motos de agua o competir en circuitos urbanos de velocidad. Una secuencia de salto en paracaídas con Lucía permite contemplar por primera vez, desde una perspectiva cenital y prácticamente en su totalidad, la descomunal escala y densidad geográfica que ofrecerá el mapa de Leónida.

articles.title: With GTA 6, Rockstar Is Ready to Prove It Can Do Romance
articles.summary: Lucia and Jason’s romance is powered by a dynamic couple system in GTA 6, but will the highs and lows of their relationship match the emotion of Arthur’s turbulent life in RDR 2?
articles.body:
We just got our most detailed look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and one thing is clear: it's a love story. One with a happy ending? That remains to be seen, but the couple dynamic alone is one of the most interesting things Rockstar Games has ever done.

It’s not that the duo of Lucia and Jason demonstrate unprecedented novelty or wild technical ambition — the series already proved it could successfully handle multiple protagonists with Trevor, Michael, and Franklin — it's that Rockstar has taken on one of the trickiest relationships to convey in gaming and made it the heart of the story. Games are notoriously bad at romance; you're either hammering simp-coded dialogue options to win the affection of another party member or watching awkward cinematics that are about as sexy as an afternoon at the podiatrist. If anyone can pull it off, though, it's Rockstar.

The new trailer shows us glimpses of Lucia and Jason working together on main story missions, but I was able to see more interesting elements of their partnership during a gameplay demo at Rockstar’s studio. In this new footage, I found that their relationship is represented in many small ways and not just them having each other’s back during bombastic shootouts. You can walk around holding hands, buy your lover a sandwich, and go shopping together to add some more clothes to your wardrobe.

"You manage the relationship in the way you hopefully nurture any relationship — which is by spending time together," Rob Nelson, Head of Development and Co-Studio Head at Rockstar North, told us. "So being in the open world and exploring together or doing activities together — playing pool or mini golf or kayaking; normal slice of life things. Or, robbing stores together, robbing banks together. However players want to spend that time together, it will have a positive impact on the relationship."

I love the introduction of a true couple dynamic. From the interactions I saw, this isn't a campaign-long escort mission or one character playing sidekick to another. They have different but equally powerful skill sets — Lucia has kickboxer training, for example — and have their own routines when apart, and so they feel like two individuals rather than one protagonist that's been hacked in half and sent on its way.

But an authentic depiction of romance is just the mechanical foundation. Being a couple working together for a taste of the good life gives the story an emotional hook that the series hasn't had before. Every crime, no matter how unhinged, is a step towards a better life together, not just one on the path towards avaricious madness. Think Bonnie and Clyde or True Romance, two people striving for the same goal, and to hell with everyone else. Suddenly, no matter how minor the crime — holding up a Waffle House or smacking around some douchebag bro type on the beach to loot him for $12 — has an emotional stake, not just a chaotic one.

The small things matter too, like staying in touch, as anyone who has ignored multiple texts from a partner while on a night out will tell you. Even if you stick to playing one character as much as possible, the other will still be out there in the world.

"You can text the other character — Jason or Lucia — at any point or you can call them. It's quite cool when you text back and forth," says Nelson.

"If you want to just spend the whole day out on your own as one of the characters, that’s fine. The other one will text you: ‘Hey, I'm going to go to bed to lock up, you OK?’ All you need to do is respond, ‘I’ll see you later,’ or, ‘OK, goodnight,’ and that's good enough. If you don't bother to even respond it may impact your relationship a bit."

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

That said, I'm pleased that engaging with the mechanics of being a couple seems to be optional in every way that matters. Their partnership is, of course, central to the narrative and so will inevitably be a component in many of the story’s missions. But the amount of effort you put into maintaining their romance and roleplaying a couple is, according to Rockstar, entirely up to you.

"Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it?” asks Nelson. “Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."

It’s the right call. Not only are romantic stories divisive — even just a few years ago I was venomously opposed to the genre — but even if you are a fan, finding couples and relationships that resonate with everyone? That's impossible. Seriously, check out the romance section of any bookstore; there's everything from cute and cuddly to monster sex. I'd rather have a GTA that no one felt alienated by than a system that forced players to smooch to finish the game.

Speaking of smooching, it sounds like Rockstar isn't going to get too down and dirty with the physical side of the relationship. Nelson explained that Rockstar didn't want to create a weird caricature of intimacy, a trap so many games have fallen into before.

"These characters feel very right together — they really do,” he says. “For anybody that wants to play around with the idea of role playing their relationship, it's amazing. So many people on the team have connected with the characters. But physical intimacy is a huge part of a relationship, and so it has to be done right. Like anything that we do, we have to iterate and try things and iterate on it until we figure out what feels right."

So Rockstar has written a couple that works on a bunch of levels, and all of them seem pretty positive at the outset. Personally, as a dark romance reader, I like my stories with a generous serving of toxicity and at least one Mafia love interest, but I think Rockstar has made the right call in giving Lucia and Jason a healthy, if felony-inclined, relationship. The world of Grand Theft Auto is one that has always welcomed experimentation, and I wouldn't want to see what the internet could come up with if it were allowed to go ham on these two precious angel babies.

"You will always have the benefit of working together and having each other's back — whether they're romantically close or not doesn't change that,” says Nelson. “They will still work together. It's really about what you want for them, their story, and how it plays out."

My only worry? As someone who cried over Red Dead Redemption 2's ending — a reaction to a game only Rockstar has ever been able to pull from my cold dead heart — there's so much potential for heartbreak no matter how much effort you put into the relationship. Rockstar likes you to make big choices — think of Niko Bellic's dilemma at the end of GTA 4 — and it's not always clear what the consequences will be until you're staring slack-jawed at the final cutscene. A couple might mean more emotionally engaging storytelling, but a couple also has so many ways to screw, screw up, or screw each other over that the risk of sobbing into my DualSense is high.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on November 19.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: GTA 6 May Be Set in Vice City, but It Has San Andreas’ Ambition
articles.summary: Rockstar reveals that San Andreas-like stats are returning in GTA 6, which tracks weight and strength based on how you eat and work out, as well as numerous other factors.
articles.body:
A return to Vice City has been a long time coming. And, from what we’ve seen of GTA 6 so far, it will at least partially feel like a homecoming for those of us who were there for Rockstar’s iconic PS2 tribute to Scarface. The 1980s may now be so far in the rear-view that our new protagonists weren’t even alive to see them, but there’s still echoes of the synthwave decade on the city’s streets: a retro Grotti Cheetah, neon-lit hotels overlooking the boardwalk, Phil Cassidy selling lethal merchandise, and a certain Vercetti Estate. It’s clear that Rockstar intends to spend at least a little time reveling in our nostalgia for Vice City.

But while it may be set in Leonida’s most immoral metropolis, what we’ve seen so far of GTA 6’s high-bar ambition suggests that it may ultimately feel more like a successor to 2004’s San Andreas than Vice City, at least in one very particular way. During a hands-off gameplay demo at Rockstar’s studio in Edinburgh, we spotted something very interesting: GTA 6 tracks an array of statistics for its two lead characters, including height, weight, sleep, nutrition, calories, shape, muscle, fat, and strength.

Rockstar North’s co-studio head, Rob Nelson, didn’t tell us much about these stats, but he did give us some minor insights into how they impact GTA 6’s overall design. “Eating has quite a dramatic effect on your health,” he revealed. “You’ll gain quite a substantial buff, so it can be useful.” He also confirmed that overeating will cause Jason and Lucia to put on weight.

“We do have gyms where you can go and work out, so you can go up in levels of muscularity or strength,” Nelson added. “You can go to the gym as Jason and Lucia together. You can go to the gym alone obviously, but if you go together, they’ll both start working out and you can get a 2-for-one to manage their stats.”

There is still much we don’t know about the system behind GTA 6’s character stats. But what I can say is that there’s a clear link between them and the RPG-style attributes that quite literally shaped San Andreas’ protagonist, CJ.

Launching just two years after Vice City, San Andreas was somehow astronomically more advanced than its predecessor despite running on the same hardware. Rather than a digital playground to commit pretend crimes in, Rockstar’s final mainline GTA of the PS2 era was a painstakingly crafted simulation of reality. At the time it was unprecedented: NPCs would comment on your appearance, car, or even odour with alarmingly authentic quips; gangs dynamically assaulted, seized, and subsequently lost turf; all 212 vehicles had their own individual physics and handling properties. The most prominent of these many sim-style ideas, though, were the bars that measured CJ’s key attributes of respect, stamina, muscle, fat, and sex appeal.

More important was the way your decisions affected those stats. Eat too many burgers and CJ would grow fat, damaging his health and running speed. Dedicate time to lifting weights and his muscles would become more defined and his punches deadlier. Push yourself on the treadmill and his stamina would increase. Wear stylish clothes and improve your personal grooming and the ladies would be more easily wooed.

These RPG-style attributes proved a little controversial back in 2004. Why would you want to hammer out all those quick-time events in the gym when you could be completing missions? Why do you need to watch your weight in a game that’s supposed to be escapist fantasy? Unsurprisingly, they were dropped for Grand Theft Auto 4 and 5. But, 14 years later, they quietly found their way into Red Dead Redemption 2, which saw Rockstar return to its ambition of a simulation-driven open world. Being over or underweight impacted Arthur Morgan’s health, making it harder to recover from wounds and regain stamina. In a world where eating food is the main source of health recovery, maintaining a balanced diet is one of RDR 2’s most unusual challenges. And now it seems a similar level of health simulation will be part of Grand Theft Auto 6, too.

Like CJ and Arthur Morgan, it appears that Lucia and Jason are characters sculpted by the activities you put them through. During our gameplay demo, we saw that running would occasionally prompt a “cardio workout” pop-up to display on screen. Food was also marked with either a heart or a lightning bolt – the very same icons used for RDR 2’s health and stamina systems. With the menu tracking the likes of calories, fat, and muscle, it seems very likely that the physical shape of our characters will be determined by what we put in their mouths and the physical movements we dictate.

Looking at both how Red Dead and San Andreas handled their respective attributes, we can guess as to what these stats tell us about GTA 6. Nutrition and calories point to every food item having some kind of numeric value that either positively or negatively impacts your protagonist’s stats, and there being some level of required nutrition to remain in “peak” condition. Calories would logically be linked to the fat stat, and so it seems sensible to expect that the weight gained from overeating will reflect the calorie content of the food we choose to eat.

However, while calories are involved in weight gain, they are also fundamental to staying alive and bulking up. I assume Rockstar isn’t leaning into the survival genre for GTA, and so you likely won’t starve to death by not eating, but I think there’s every chance you’ll need to eat to allow your characters to build muscle and strength when at the gym – the very inclusion of which point to a return of the exercise mini-games from San Andreas.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Finally, the sleep stat points to the idea that we may well need to get some shut-eye to stay in good condition. Perhaps, like RDR 2, regular sleep will keep our key stat “cores” (or GTA’s equivalent) topped up and allow us to recover health and stamina over time without the need to find restorative items.

It’s a risky business to include this kind of stat-driven simulation in what will undoubtedly be the most mass-market video game of all time. The average GTA 6 player likely won’t even know their character attributes are there, never mind that they’re tracked and actively change their in-world avatars. It’s backfired before, and it’s likely that GTA 6’s stats will be much more complex and nuanced than San Andreas’ controversial attributes. But, considering the triumph that was Red Dead Redemption 2’s unparalleled simulation of life in the old west, I can’t wait to see how Rockstar have applied those ideas to a couple of criminals trying to make a living in Vice City.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: GTA 6 Just Blew Me Away; I'm So Glad I Avoided the Leaks
articles.summary: There were a ton of GTA 6 leaks before the Netflix Extended Look, and I'm glad I avoided them, because it looks absolutely incredible.
articles.body:
I'm so, so glad I avoided the GTA 6 leaks . Grand Theft Auto has been one of my favorite franchises since GTA 3 convinced me to buy a PS2 with its paradigm-shifting open-world gameplay. That's continued with every major release since, most recently with 2013's Grand Theft Auto 5, which I personally regard as one of the ten greatest games ever made.

So to say I've been hyped up for GTA 6 – and for today’s Extended Look – would be putting it mildly. Thirteen years is a long time between entries (for context, the previous longest wait between mainline entries was the five years between 4 and 5), and though Rockstar made a generationally incredible game in the intervening years in the form of Red Dead Redemption 2, I've always been more of a GTA guy.

When the clock struck 12pm, I hit Play on Netflix. My jaw hit the floor very quickly, and I didn't pick it back up for 27 minutes. The first thing that jumped out at me was the lighting. The softness of the dynamic lighting added a layer of realism to what's on the screen in a way that is simultaneously both subtle and jarring with how much it adds to every scene. And I do mean every scene, from the grimy apartment building the demo starts out in to the rooftop bar under the golden glow of Vice City's afternoon sunshine, the lighting was the first "holy sh*t" moment for me.

The next thing that floored me – and again, it's kind of subtle – is the UI, or rather, the lack of it. At first I thought Rockstar had it turned off to add to the cinematic flair of this Extended Look, but it turns out that, nope, it was on the whole time. Instead, Rockstar has stripped the UI to the bare minimum in order to add to the realism that the absolutely insane graphics produce. Small, simple prompts appear only when needed. And yes, the classic GTA mini-map still lives in the lower-left corner of the screen, but apparently only when you're out in the open world. I absolutely adore this minimalist approach to UI.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

How about the attention to detail? My goodness it was everywhere. Jason doesn't just pet the dog, it jumps up on his legs. Jason and Lucia hold hands when heading to a meeting. Lucia's blood splatters on the wall behind her when she gets attacked, but not in the usual comically over-the-top way we see in video games. The way the BMW look-alike's convertible top retracted back after our anti-heroes started driving. I could go on and on just from this 27-minute demo.

Since I've purposely avoided the leaks, I still have no idea how large Leonida is, and I don't want to know until I finally get my hands on it in 84 days from now (not that I'm counting or anything...). There is so much left to discover and soak in. And that’s the best part.

For me, a huge part of the reason I love Grand Theft Auto so much is that it has continually raised the bar for what's possible in a blockbuster video game. What other developers – even incredibly talented ones – at other studios can't do, Rockstar can. Because Rockstar doesn't have a limited budget. It doesn't have limited time. The runaway success of its catalog of games, which very much includes the money-printing ATM that is GTA 5 Online, allows them to say yes to everything and say no to nothing.

One of my favorite anecdotes from my time playing GTA 5 is the odd shuttle bus I once stumbled upon in Vinewood. Pressing Y to board it, my Michael sat down and a "tour of the stars' homes" started, complete with voiced narration by a tour guide. This wasn't a mission. It wasn't marked on the map. I imagine that the majority of players never find it, because it's not called out in any way. Our first proper look at GTA 6 suggests that there are probably going to be a lot more things like that hiding inside of Leonida.

I have played thousands of games in my life, and I have never seen anything like Grand Theft Auto 6. Somehow, my sky-high expectations and hype level have been not only met but exceeded. Let's all enjoy this moment, both now and when we finally get our hands on this thing on November 19. They don't come around very often.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Star Citizen Spinoff Squadron 42 Delayed to 2027, Dev Insists It's Because of GTA 6
articles.summary: Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6.
articles.body:
Star Citizen single-player spinoff Squadron 42 has been delayed to 2027, with developer Chris Roberts insisting it wouldn't get the attention it deserves because of Grand Theft Auto 6.

In a new blog post, Cloud Imperium Games CEO Chris Roberts announced that Squadron 42 will be launching in Q2 2027. The studio had previously announced 2026 as its release window and reaffirmed late last year that it was still targeting that . However, Roberts noted that GTA 6 is going to suck up all of the attention this fall, and as a result, it doesn't make sense to launch a new game during that time.

"At CitizenCon 2024, we announced we would ship in 2026. Our plan was to release in Q4 around IAE," said Roberts. "But much like the rest of the industry there is no way I want to launch my spiritual successor to Wing Commander, a game that has had twelve years of blood, sweat and tears invested into it (we started Squadron 42 development in 2014 as 2013 was opening studios, hiring people and getting the Hangar module out for Star Citizen) launching into the attention buzz saw of GTA 6. While GTA 6 isn’t launching on PC this November, pretty much all outlets and most content creators will be all over it, not leaving a lot of room for other coverage."

Roberts went on to note that CIG will be doing previews of Squadron 42 with content creators and early backers in October, which it will use as an opportunity to announce release plans with a concrete date to follow "shortly" afterwards. Q2 would place Squadron 42 sometime during the spring, so long as nothing changes between now and then.

Squadron 42 has been in development for over a decade now, almost as long as Star Citizen itself. The game has been delayed numerous times, but promises an ambitious story and gameplay experience. It also boasts an absurdly star-studded cast including Gary Oldman, Mark Hamill, Henry Cavill, Andy Serkis, Ben Mendelsohn, Mark Strong, and many, many others. The cast may have expanded well beyond those names over the years as well.

Roberts had also previously stated that he hopes that Squadron 42's release will be as big of an event as GTA 6 , noting that it's probably the biggest-budget game behind Rockstar's open-world crime epic. Star Citizen crossed the $1 billion mark earlier this year when it comes to funding , and there aren't many other games that can rival a budget like that.

The delay announcement comes hot on the heels of a disastrous Star Citizen developer livestream that went radically off the rails . After early access players complained of bugs and issues with a new update to the game, the developers held a stream to show the "intended" version of the experience, only to be met with the same issues, if not worse. It led to passive-aggressive comments between the developers themselves and an uncomfortable tension in the air. Many have wondered if Star Citizen will ever actually properly release and that broadcast didn't help with those concerns.

Star Citzen itself remains without a release window.

articles.title: GTA 6 Devs at Rockstar Celebrate as Extended Look Finally Reveals Gameplay After Years of Development

articles.body:
Rockstar Games has finally revealed an official look at Grand Theft Auto 6 gameplay, and members of the development team couldn't be happier to finally see fans' reactions.

Our first real glimpse at what the GTA 6 studio has been cooking up finally arrived as part of the Netflix extended look today. While there's still plenty of side activities , romance subplots , and robberies for Jason and Lucia that we've yet to see, the developers at Rockstar are just happy their work can be shown off as intended.

"Our Teams across the World have worked incredibly hard," production designer Terrance Radcliff said . "So proud of everyone. Watching this with coworkers as a Family – and when I get home I’ll watch again with my Family!"

"The first ever game I have played was Vice City as a kid," graphic programmer Mert Kirimgeri said . "It's an honour to be working with the most professional, brilliant and kind people on the planet over the most immersive game ever made, not to mention one of the most complex computer systems in human existence. Enjoy!!!"

"Watching this with my colleagues was such an emotional experience," associate principal 3D graphic artist Sara Lazzeroni said . "I've seen quite a few teary eyes. I've spent a quarter of my life working hard on this game and there are no words to express how moving it is to see it all come together and share it with you all."

GTA 6 reportedly truly began development in 2020 and was announced in 2022 . After a leak , the trailer then officially made its way online with a first look at Jason and Lucia in December 2023.

articles.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 Gameplay Just Makes Me Want a PC Version Even More
articles.summary: After watching the Grand Theft Auto 6 Extended Look on Netflix, I came away awed by how good it looks on the base consoles. But more than anything, it made me want to see it running on a high-end PC even more.
articles.body:
I wasn't exactly surprised when I heard that Grand Theft Auto 6 would be coming to PS5 and Xbox Series X before it ever comes to PC ; Rockstar took that same approach with GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 . Even though I've had to wait for those games to come to PC, they've always been better when you have the hardware to really push these games to another level, and I didn't expect GTA 6 to be any different.

Then I watched the Extended Look on Netflix, and it looks incredible. Even from from my couch, I could tell there were some incredible ray-traced global illumination, reflection, and shadow effects, which really make the game come alive. There were even moments — like when Jason and Lucia talk to someone behind a window — where the shadows dynamically move across the stranger's face that really make the game look like a technical masterpiece.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

The only problem is that it was running on a base PS5 . The game looks incredible regardless, but there were certainly moments where the frame rate slowed down considerably. I had already heard word that GTA 6 will only get a 60fps mode on the PS5 Pro , and now I can definitely see why. With all those lighting effects and the high-resolution textures, Grand Theft Auto 6 is really going to make the base consoles chug .

I have a hard time believing that GTA 6 will even be able to run at a steady 60fps on even the PS5 Pro, even though I know just how talented Rockstar's engineers are at making gorgeous games run on limited hardware. What I really want to do is take away those limits with an extemely powerful graphics card .

When Red Dead Redemption 2 finally made its way to PC, it was one my go-to games to test hardware with for years. I've only just recently dropped it from my testing rotation. The reason it stuck around so long was how scalable it was. Rockstar found a way to allow people to turn the settings down to a ridiculous degree, to be able to play it on PCs that frankly had no right trying to run it. Likewise, if you did have a beefy computer, there were dozens of things you could tweak that elevated the game far beyond how it looked on the PS4 and Xbox One. That game's PC port was a huge leap over GTA 5's port, too, and I suspect that when GTA 6 makes its way to PC (maybe sometime next year?), Rockstar is going to take those learnings even further.

There are already a couple things I'd like to see from the PC version. In a couple of moments in the extended trailer, reflections were quite noisy, particularly in the bodies of cars. It just so happens that Nvidia launched a new version of ray reconstruction just this week at Gamescom that would basically solve that issue.

At least until some new version of GTA Online comes out, this would be the perfect game to use frame generation, which will help smooth out some of the more noticeable frame drops — at least visually. I know that frame generation is controversial, but this is one of those games where I really want to see just how smooth I can make it, especially because the world looks so lived-in otherwise.

I'm sure there are plenty of folks out there that really just want to get their hands on the game immediately. And while I'll probably end up playing it at least a little bit when the game launches on consoles in November, I just know that I'm going to want to wait until the game launches on PC to really dive in.

Who knows, there may even be more powerful graphics hardware available when the PC version launches that will make the game look even better than what's possible right now. I don't know what the PC version of the game is going to look like yet, of course, but I know that once it finally comes out I'm going to put it through its paces to see just how good I can get it looking — maybe even with mods.

If it looks as good on PS5 as it the Netflix Extended Look made it seem, the inevitable PC port is going to be absolutely jaw-dropping. I already wanted that PC port, but now I need it.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Pokémon Responds After Hacker Compromises Its X Account to Hawk MemeCoin
articles.summary: The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin.
articles.body:
The official Pokémon profile on X has responded after its account was hacked by an unknown party who shared a post linking out to a memecoin.

The hack occurred around 3 PM PT on August 17, 2026. The post — which has since been deleted — was cleverly structured, appearing as an official Pokémon advertisement with a link to a site that, at first glance, looked like a legitimate page celebrating the brand’s 30th anniversary, which is ongoing.

“Celebrate 30 years of Pokémon in a whole new way!” the post read. “Introducing $POKEMON, the official Pokemon memecoin. Join trainers around the world and be part of the #Pokemon30 celebration.”

The post was up for around thirty minutes before it was finally taken down. Most commenters weren’t fooled, though, and it wasn’t long before proposed community notes began appearing underneath the supposed scam on X.

Pokémon published a statement addressing the hack shortly afterward, acknowledging that the account had been compromised for a thirty-minute period.

“We’re aware that our X account was accessed without authorization and used to publish posts promoting a cryptocurrency,” it wrote. “Those posts were not created or approved by Pokémon and have been removed. We have secured the account and are investigating the incident. We’re sorry for the confusion and appreciate your patience.”

The @Pokemon handle on X was temporarily compromised earlier for ~30 minutes. We’re aware that our X account was accessed without authorization and used to publish posts promoting a cryptocurrency. Those posts were not created or approved by Pokémon and have been removed. We… — Pokémon (@Pokemon) August 27, 2026

The @Pokemon handle on X was temporarily compromised earlier for ~30 minutes. We’re aware that our X account was accessed without authorization and used to publish posts promoting a cryptocurrency. Those posts were not created or approved by Pokémon and have been removed. We…

Fans flooded the comments underneath this post with relief, along with endless memes joking that Team Rocket must've been behind the hack. However, this post was also deleted shortly after being published, and no follow-up remarks have yet been made on the account regarding the hack.

It's unclear if any damage was done as a result of the incident, but this wouldn't be the first time the brand has been digitally infiltrated; in late 2024, a hacker performed one of the largest leaks of Pokémon materials in history after servers at developer GameFreak were breached.

What resulted was "hundreds of gigabytes to nearly a terabyte" of internal data getting spread around the net, which reportedly included concept art, unused Pokémon prototoypes, source code, and even codenames for planned future games.

And in 2025, hackers released Pokémon Legends: Z-A files that included gameplay videos showing cut content and early builds of the game.

Thankfully, this latest incident wasn't nearly as terrifying as either of those two hacks, and the official Pokémon account is far from the first profile on X to get hijacked by cryptocoin scammers... though that isn't exactly a comforting thought. In fact, the hacker behind the infamous GTA 6 leaks has also hawked a crypto scheme, though the gameplay footage they showed pales in comparison to the viral Netflix showcase that aired on the platform earlier today.

articles.title: The X-Tech Executive Chair Aims to Upend Premium Models from Herman Miller, Steelcase at a Better Price
articles.summary: Battle of the super premium tier chairs.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This article is sponsored by X-Chair.

X-Chair's "top of the line" office chair - the X-Tech Executive - retails for $1,845, although it's currently on sale for $1,384. That places this chair firmly in the super premium tier. As far as ergonomic chairs go, the rule of "you get what you pay for" is fairly accurate, most of the time. High quality chairs are really expensive for a reason. And for people who spend several hours per day sitting, whether it be for work or for gaming marathons, the investment is justifiable.

At first glance, the X-Tech Executive looks like a typical office chair. It's not gaudy like some of the racing-styled gaming chairs out there. This is actually X-Chair's roomiest chair, with a 22" seat width and up to 275 pound weight capacity. X-Chair states on its page that the chair is best suited for medium to large-framed people.

The seat is made of a supportive cooling memory foam that contours to your body. The seat and upper back section are upholstered in Brisa performance faux-leather fabric that's both breathable and easily washable. The lower back is made of a flexible mesh material which X-Chair calls "adaptive thermoregulating (ATR)".

In terms of ergonomics, the X-Tech Executive features a dynamic variable lumbar system. The lower back is disconnected from the rest of the chair and adjusts automatically based on your movement. That way, your back is supported no matter what position you might be in. This dynamic lumbar foregoes your need to manually adjust the settings.

If you're going to spend this much for a chair, then you should definitely pay an extra $50 for the optional X-HMT heat massager. This add-on is seamlessly incorporated into the lower back section for some much welcome therapy. This upgrade isn't available in most ergonomic chairs and when it is, it can cost upwards of $300. For just 3% of the cost of the entire chair, I see no reason why anyone would opt out of the upgrade.

The X-Tech Executive is clearly targeted towards professionals who are looking at premium options from brands like Herman Miller, Steelcase, and Haworth, among others. The best chairs from these brands, however, are priced even higher; for example, the Herman Miller Embody is listed at $2,000. Compared to these options, the X-Tech Executive is actually a more reasonably priced high-end alternative that promises the same level of both comfort and ergonomics.

articles.title: The biggest video game of all time looks like a movie
articles.summary: Rockstar’s “extended look” at GTA VI, which debuted first on Netflix, felt like a slice of a prestige crime drama, with the studio clearly trying to further blur the lines between Hollywood and video games.
articles.body: I think I know why Rockstar Games debuted its “extended look” of Grand Theft Auto VI on Netflix instead of immediately dropping it for free on YouTube. Unlike most video game trailers, the almost 27-minute preview of GTA VI felt more like a slice of a prestige crime drama than any video game trailer that I’ve ever seen. To make a new game that lasts another decade or more and potentially rivals the success of its predecessor, Rockstar is clearly trying to further blur the lines between Hollywood and video games. The line between games and movies has been getting consistently fuzzier. Look no further than this year’s James Bond game, 007 First Light, which has the snappy pacing, acting, and cinematography of a great action film. And TV shows and movies are increasingly pulling from video games for inspiration, to say nothing of entire TV and movie franchises being built around successful video games. Now, a video game trailer has wedged between prestige TV and streaming hit movies — after watching the GTA VI preview, Netflix is suggesting I watch Breaking Bad next. Rockstar is keeping GTA VI’s plot details close to its chest, but the video gives the broad strokes: GTA VI is about protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos working together in Vice City. Across the tightly-edited video, which jumps between cutscenes and moments of actual gameplay, Jason and Lucia do a lot of GTA-style crimes: they evade cops in gunfights, pull off high-stakes robberies, and shoot a lot of people. But they also have moments of chatting leisurely in the car or even bickering about what clothes to wear. The video also isn’t just an uninterrupted vertical section of gameplay, like video game deep dives often are. Instead, it artistically cuts between different sections, storylines, and characters to paint a picture of what to expect. I didn’t always know what was going on, but by the end of the video, I had a sense of who these people were and the city that they live in. It felt, well, like parts of a movie. GTA VI will still be very much a video game. Rockstar invited a handful of outlets to preview GTA VI, and their coverage dives into things like the expansive map, the six-star Wanted system, escalating requirements to steal cars, and reactive NPCs. Those will almost certainly make for a vast sandbox to play in, building on the already immersive worlds of previous Rockstar games like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. For GTA VI’s extended look, Rockstar instead opted to show setup, action, and dialogue scenes, leaning on story and atmosphere over gameplay mechanics. It’s a cinematic choice. Maybe I’m thinking too deeply about a video game trailer. Yes, I know that part of this Netflix video is all just marketing hype — and Netflix probably saw it as a way to get new subscribers. And the trailer isn’t only available on Netflix; Rockstar let creators share reaction videos and is publishing the extended look on its YouTube channel and its own website at 9PM ET. But expectations are high for GTA VI. 13-year-old GTA V has sold more than 230 million copies, making it one of the top-selling games of all time. Rockstar’s previous two trailers for GTA VI have racked up hundreds of millions of views. GTA Online is a big cash cow in its own right, too. But Rockstar can always do more with a game many years in the making that might be fighting for time with the Netflix library. If Thursday’s preview was any indication, all those titles might get real competition when GTA VI launches on November 19th.

During a recent hands-off demo of GTA 6 at Rockstar HQ, we spotted the quiet return of something that hasn’t been a major part of the series for over twenty years. But we’re not talking about big perms and leg warmers, we’re talking about body building.

Before the dizzying realism of Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA San Andreas was undoubtedly Rockstar’s most ambitious game: a deep world simulation with an array of RPG stats and character customisation options that had an impact on the gameplay and were noticed by the game’s reactive NPCs. The system was well ahead of its time, though many players bounced off it. Often on the grounds that watching your diet and going to the gym in real life isn’t fun, so it shouldn’t be a mandatory minigame in an escapist fantasy.

Well, Rockstar have decided to bring it all back for GTA 6: you can take Jason and Lucia to the gym, alone or together, to work on their lats and six-packs. And, yes, you can overeat to make them fat, which might not be great for outrunning the cops but it is very funny. Who’d have thought that one of GTA 6’s most exciting innovations would be all about lifting things and putting them back down again.

articles.title: The Whisper Man Is a Trope-Heavy Thriller Starring Robert De Niro and Adam Scott That Feels Like a Throwback to Another Era
articles.summary: The Whisper Man review: Robert De Niro and Adam Scott headline a trope-heavy thriller that feels like a throwback to another era.
articles.body:
The Whisper Man premieres globally on Netflix on August 28.

Tragedy. Fathers desperate for connection with their sons and failing to find it. A string of murders that left a town shaken and an eerie nursery rhyme in their wake. Minds, homes, and families haunted. A cop desperate to stop the murder of a small boy before it happens. The Whisper Man has all the ingredients of a story that will chill your bones.

Based on the novel by Alex North, the film follows newly widowed crime novelist Tom Kennedy (Adam Scott), who is forced to reconcile with estranged father and retired detective Pete Willis (Robert De Niro) when his son Jake (Acston Luca Porto) goes missing. The kidnapping follows the pattern of a child abduction and murder spree that Willis solved when Tom was just a boy; the circumstances of Willis’ involvement with the crime and its perpetrator left the detective so traumatized that he ultimately abandoned his family.

The only person who might know who is behind these grisly acts — a butcher of innocents known as the Whisper Man — sits rotting in the jail cell where Willis put him. Desperate to find Jake and assigned to the case, Detective Amanda Beck (Michelle Monaghan) joins forces with Willis in a partnership that’s one of several contrivances meant to move the plot along. Unfortunately, that team doesn’t always track, and the circumstances surrounding the home that Tom rents are so full of wild coincidences that one is left utterly baffled.

The Whisper Man draws on a hodgepodge of influences, tropes, and plotlines from past thrillers, some more successful than others. James Patterson’s serial killer novels, Slender Man, The Silence of the Lambs, The Sixth Sense, The Black Phone, and A Nightmare on Elm Street’s Freddy Krueger all shape the story; there are even shades of the Pied Piper in the mix. It’s a potentially potent mix, but as much as The Whisper Man aims to shock, the largest reveal is telegraphed fairly early on, leaving the viewer to wait for the film to catch up.

The base premise is inherently horrific, and director James Ashcroft (Coming Home in the Dark) delivers unsettling images and auditory motifs, but the central relationships — Tom and his father; Jake and Tom; and Willis and his nemesis, the Whisper Man — aren’t fleshed out enough to leave a deep imprint because valuable screen time that could develop those emotional stakes is instead spent on a series of side stories and characters that mostly muddle the plot.

In a world where filmmakers regularly play with and reinvent the horror genre, this one feels like it was lifted from a time capsule. Retro can have its appeal, and The Whisper Man moves along at a brisk, fairly engaging pace. But the major outcomes are foreseeable, and the surprising moments are often just bits of plotting that make no sense. The film serves up curveballs that don’t land, befuddling character choices, obvious red herrings, and one wildly disturbing villain motivation that the film absolutely doesn’t earn. While serviceably directed with some effective and entertaining moments and a remarkably stacked cast that delivers a couple of scene-chewing interactions, The Whisper Man is too full of unexplored threads and illogical turns to pay off its promise.

articles.title: How the GTA 6 Map Size Stacks Up to Other Rockstar Games Like RDR2 and GTA 5
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than Rockstar's previous games; here's how it compares to the studio's other titles.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6's map is significantly larger than the maps in Rockstar's previous games. Here's how it compares to the studio's other titles, according to the developer.

Rockstar Games confirmed to The New York Times and YouTuber TGG that Grand Theft Auto 6's map is three times bigger than the playable area of Red Dead Redemption 2. Elaborating to TGG, it was revealed that it is twice the size of Grand Theft Auto 5, and Vice City itself is twice the size of Los Santos from GTA 5. Vice City and its surrounding suburbs are 11 times bigger than Los Santos and its surrounding areas.

If that wasn't enough for you, TGG also revealed that there are "hundreds" of accessible interiors in GTA 6. In GTA 5, players could enter the homes of their respective characters, different shops, and a few random buildings like the Los Santos police station, but generally speaking, there weren't a lot of places you could enter. GTA Online has added more over time, but they often require loading screens and are very restrictive.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

The GTA 6 extended look already showed off a variety of interiors both inside and outside of missions, so that should make Leonida a lot more layered. Speaking to IGN , Rockstar Games' Rob Nelson discussed how the developer took lessons learned from building Red Dead Redemption 2's version of the Wild West and expanded upon those ideas with GTA 6.

“I think with Red Dead Redemption 2, we finally had the team and the tech and then took the time we needed to push the idea of making a fully realized consistent-feeling world further than we ever had,” Nelson explained.

“With that game we took the time necessary to take advantage of that generation of hardware to maximize the quality of our open world population, design, and gameplay so that when you were riding from here to there in-game, you were constantly getting distracted and pulled in different directions. And then you could really get lost as that character in that place. That's when to me, these games can feel magical and create a sense of wonder that the world is alive – and you get these little shivers of ‘What’s happening?’

"GTA 6 is a continuation of our team pushing in this direction – doing everything we possibly can to create the largest, deepest, most densely populated and complex world we have ever built for people to get lost in.”
